        example = """
            SCHEMA = {
                "name": "send_email",
                "params": {
                    "to": {"type": str, "required": True},
                    "subject": {"type": str, "required": True},
                    "priority": {"type": int, "required": False, "allowed": [1, 2, 3]},
                },
            }

            def check_call(schema, arguments):
                problems = []
                for name, rule in schema["params"].items():
                    if name not in arguments:
                        if rule["required"]:
                            problems.append(f"missing {name}")
                        continue
                    value = arguments[name]
                    if not isinstance(value, rule["type"]):
                        problems.append(f"{name} must be {rule['type'].__name__}")
                    elif "allowed" in rule and value not in rule["allowed"]:
                        problems.append(f"{name} must be one of {rule['allowed']}")
                for name in arguments:
                    if name not in schema["params"]:
                        problems.append(f"unknown argument {name}")
                return problems

            calls = [
                {"to": "ann@example.com", "subject": "Build passed", "priority": 2},
                {"to": "ann@example.com", "priority": 9},
                {"to": 42, "subject": "Hi", "cc": "bob@example.com"},
            ]
            for arguments in calls:
                problems = check_call(SCHEMA, arguments)
                print("ok" if not problems else "rejected: " + "; ".join(problems))
        """,
    ),

        details = "The example writes three events, verifies the chain, changes one event and verifies again. The second check reports the first broken entry.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as hash_chain.py.
            2. Run it: python3 hash_chain.py
        """,
        example = """
            import hashlib

            def digest(previous, event):
                return hashlib.sha256((previous + event).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]

            def append(log, event):
                previous = log[-1]["hash"] if log else "0" * 8
                log.append({"event": event, "hash": digest(previous, event)})

            def verify(log):
                previous = "0" * 8
                for index, entry in enumerate(log):
                    if entry["hash"] != digest(previous, entry["event"]):
                        return f"broken at entry {index}"
                    previous = entry["hash"]
                return "chain intact"

            log = []
            for event in ["agent read retry.md", "agent wrote notes.txt", "agent sent report"]:
                append(log, event)
            print(verify(log))
            log[1]["event"] = "agent deleted notes.txt"
            print(verify(log))
        """,
    ),
)

/** Flex pieces of 2026 to 2036: a signature that needs only a hash, a derivative in a few dozen lines, and a space-filling curve. */
val db9Flex: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 9,
        kind = Kind.FLEX,
        section = "Signatures",
        title = "A hash-based one-time signature",
        originalTitle = "Constructing digital signatures from a one-way function (Lamport, 1979)",
        author = "Leslie Lamport",
        year = 2030,
        summary = "Signs a message using only a hash function: the key is 512 secret values, and each bit of the message reveals one of them.",
        details = "Hash-based signatures do not rely on factoring or elliptic curves, so a quantum computer does not break them. This version signs one message per key, and the example checks a signature and then a changed message.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as lamport.py.
            2. Run it: python3 lamport.py
        """,
        example = """
            import hashlib

            def H(data):
                return hashlib.sha256(data).digest()

            def keygen(seed):
                # Two secret values per bit of the digest, derived from the seed so the example is repeatable.
                pairs = []
                for i in range(256):
                    zero = H(seed + i.to_bytes(2, "big") + b"0")
                    one = H(seed + i.to_bytes(2, "big") + b"1")
                    pairs.append((zero, one))
                public = [(H(zero), H(one)) for zero, one in pairs]
                return pairs, public

            def bits(message):
                digest = H(message)
                return [(digest[i // 8] >> (7 - i % 8)) & 1 for i in range(256)]

            def sign(secret, message):
                return [secret[i][bit] for i, bit in enumerate(bits(message))]

            def verify(public, message, signature):
                return all(H(signature[i]) == public[i][bit] for i, bit in enumerate(bits(message)))

            secret, public = keygen(b"demo seed")
            signature = sign(secret, b"pay Ann 10")
            print("valid:", verify(public, b"pay Ann 10", signature))
            print("changed message:", verify(public, b"pay Ann 1000", signature))
        """,
    ),

    entry(
        databaseId = 9,
        kind = Kind.FLEX,
        section = "Autodiff",
        title = "Reverse-mode differentiation in 30 lines",
        originalTitle = "Automatic derivative evaluation (Wengert, 1964)",
        author = "Robert Wengert",
        year = 2027,
        summary = "Records each addition and multiplication, then walks the record backwards to get the derivative of the result with respect to each input.",
        details = "This is the mechanism behind training neural networks, in miniature. The example differentiates a small expression of two inputs and prints the result and both derivatives.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as autodiff.py.
            2. Run it: python3 autodiff.py
        """,
        example = """
            class Value:
                def __init__(self, data, parents=(), backward=None):
                    self.data = data
                    self.grad = 0.0
                    self.parents = parents
                    self.backward = backward

                def __add__(self, other):
                    other = other if isinstance(other, Value) else Value(other)
                    out = Value(self.data + other.data, (self, other))
                    def backward():
                        self.grad += out.grad
                        other.grad += out.grad
                    out.backward = backward
                    return out

                def __mul__(self, other):
                    other = other if isinstance(other, Value) else Value(other)
                    out = Value(self.data * other.data, (self, other))
                    def backward():
                        self.grad += other.data * out.grad
                        other.grad += self.data * out.grad
                    out.backward = backward
                    return out

                def backprop(self):
                    order, seen = [], set()
                    def visit(node):
                        if id(node) not in seen:
                            seen.add(id(node))
                            for parent in node.parents:
                                visit(parent)
                            order.append(node)
                    visit(self)
                    self.grad = 1.0
                    for node in reversed(order):
                        if node.backward:
                            node.backward()

            x = Value(3.0)
            y = Value(2.0)
            f = x * y + y * x          # f = 2xy
            f.backprop()
            print("f =", f.data)
            print("df/dx =", x.grad)
            print("df/dy =", y.grad)
        """,
    ),

        databaseId = 9,
        kind = Kind.FLEX,

        author = "David Hilbert",
        year = 2032,
        summary = "Gives each cell of a square grid a position along a curve that keeps neighbouring cells close, which helps spatial indexes and data layout.",
        details = "The example computes the index of each cell of a four by four grid and prints the grid. Consecutive indexes always sit in neighbouring cells.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as hilbert.py.
            2. Run it: python3 hilbert.py
        """,
        example = """
            def xy2d(n, x, y):
                # Position of cell (x, y) along the Hilbert curve that fills an n by n grid (n a power of two).
                d = 0
                s = n // 2
                while s > 0:
                    rx = 1 if x & s else 0
                    ry = 1 if y & s else 0
                    d += s * s * ((3 * rx) ^ ry)
                    if ry == 0:
                        if rx == 1:
                            x = n - 1 - x
                            y = n - 1 - y
                        x, y = y, x
                    s //= 2
                return d

            for y in range(3, -1, -1):
                print(" ".join(f"{xy2d(4, x, y):2}" for x in range(4)))
        """,
    ),
)

            class Token:
                def __init__(self, holder, scopes, expires_at):
                    self.holder = holder
                    self.scopes = set(scopes)
                    self.expires_at = expires_at

            def check(token, scope, now):
                # A call is allowed only if the token has not expired and names the scope.
                if now >= token.expires_at:
                    return False, "expired"
                if scope not in token.scopes:
                    return False, "scope not granted"
                return True, "ok"

            for now, scope in [(10, "search"), (20, "read"), (30, "send"), (100, "read")]:

        details = "This is the grow-only counter. Each replica increments only its own slot, and a merge takes the maximum of each slot, so merges in any order give the same total. The example merges three replicas in two orders and checks that the results match.",
        instructions = """

        example = """
            def increment(counter, replica):
                counter = dict(counter)
                counter[replica] = counter.get(replica, 0) + 1
                return counter

            def merge(a, b):
                # Each replica's slot takes the larger value, so the order of merges does not matter.
                return {r: max(a.get(r, 0), b.get(r, 0)) for r in set(a) | set(b)}

            def total(counter):
                return sum(counter.values())

            # Three replicas count while they are apart.
            a = increment(increment({}, "a"), "a")                       # a: 2
            b = increment({}, "b")                                       # b: 1
            c = increment(increment(increment({}, "c"), "c"), "c")       # c: 3

            left = merge(merge(a, b), c)
            right = merge(c, merge(b, a))
            print(sorted(left.items()), total(left))
            print(sorted(right.items()), total(right))
            print("same result:", left == right)
        """,

                # Extract a fixed-length key from the input, then expand it to the length asked for (RFC 5869).
                prk = hmac.new(salt, ikm, hashlib.sha256).digest()
                okm = b""
                block = b""

        instructions = """

        example = """
            class TokenBucket:
                def __init__(self, capacity, refill_per_second):
                    self.capacity = capacity
                    self.refill = refill_per_second
                    self.tokens = capacity
                    self.last = 0.0

                def allow(self, now):
                    # Refill for the time since the last call, up to the bucket size, then spend one token.
                    self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + (now - self.last) * self.refill)
                    self.last = now
                    if self.tokens >= 1:
                        self.tokens -= 1
                        return True
                    return False

            bucket = TokenBucket(capacity=3, refill_per_second=1.0)
            calls = [0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1.2, 1.3, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8]
            print(" ".join("yes" if bucket.allow(t) else "no" for t in calls))
        """,

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Projects of 2026 to 2036: small programs for local-first sync, carbon-aware scheduling, agent permissions and bills of materials. */
val db9Projects: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 9,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Local-first",
        title = "A to-do list that syncs two replicas",
        originalTitle = "A last-writer-wins map, as in local-first apps",
        author = "Written as a teaching example",
        year = 2030,
        summary = "Two replicas of a to-do list change offline and merge in either direction, and both end with the same list.",
        details = "Each item keeps the clock of its last change and whether it is on the list. A merge keeps the newer entry for each item, so the result is the same in either direction. The example runs the scenario and prints both lists.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as todo_sync.py.
            2. Run it: python3 todo_sync.py
        """,
        example = """
            class Replica:
                def __init__(self, name):
                    self.name = name
                    self.items = {}      # item -> (clock of its last change, on the list?)
                    self.clock = 0

                def set(self, item, on_list):
                    self.clock += 1
                    self.items[item] = (self.clock, on_list)

                def merge(self, other):
                    # The entry with the newer clock wins, whichever replica it came from.
                    for item, entry in other.items.items():
                        if item not in self.items or entry > self.items[item]:
                            self.items[item] = entry

                def todo(self):
                    return sorted(item for item, (_, on_list) in self.items.items() if on_list)

            phone = Replica("phone")
            laptop = Replica("laptop")

            phone.set("milk", True)
            laptop.merge(phone)              # the laptop has seen the milk
            phone.set("bread", True)         # offline edits from here on
            phone.set("milk", False)         # bought it
            laptop.set("eggs", True)
            laptop.set("tea", True)
            laptop.set("bread", False)       # crossed off on the laptop

            phone.merge(laptop)
            laptop.merge(phone)
            print("phone:", phone.todo())
            print("laptop:", laptop.todo())
            print("same:", phone.todo() == laptop.todo())
        """,
    ),

    entry(
        databaseId = 9,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Green software",
        title = "A carbon-aware job scheduler",
        originalTitle = "Scheduling jobs into the cleanest hours",
        author = "Written as a teaching example",
        year = 2029,
        summary = "Places each job in the window with the lowest grid carbon intensity that still meets its deadline, then reports the plan.",
        details = "The example takes 24 hourly intensity values and three jobs with deadlines. It places the heaviest job first, then the others, and prints the start hour and the carbon estimate of each.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as scheduler.py.
            2. Run it: python3 scheduler.py
        """,
        example = """
            # Grid carbon intensity in grams of CO2 per kWh, for each hour of the day starting at midnight.
            intensity = [400, 380, 300, 260, 240, 230, 250, 290, 360, 400, 420, 430,
                         410, 390, 350, 310, 280, 270, 300, 350, 400, 420, 430, 440]

            # Each job: name, hours it needs, kWh used per hour, and the hour by which it must finish.
            jobs = [("report", 1, 0.5, 6), ("backup", 2, 1.5, 8), ("training", 3, 4.0, 24)]

            free = [True] * 24
            schedule = []
            total = 0.0
            for name, hours, kwh, deadline in sorted(jobs, key=lambda job: -job[2]):   # heaviest first
                best = None
                for start in range(deadline - hours + 1):
                    block = range(start, start + hours)
                    if all(free[h] for h in block):
                        cost = sum(intensity[h] for h in block) * kwh
                        if best is None or cost < best[0]:
                            best = (cost, start)
                cost, start = best
                for h in range(start, start + hours):
                    free[h] = False
                total += cost
                schedule.append((name, start, round(cost)))

            for name, start, grams in sorted(schedule, key=lambda entry: entry[1]):
                print(f"{name}: start at {start:02d}:00, {grams} g CO2")
            print(f"total: {round(total)} g CO2")
        """,
    ),

    entry(
        databaseId = 9,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Agents",
        title = "A permission checker for agents",
        originalTitle = "Deny-first policies for tool calls",
        author = "Written as a teaching example",
        year = 2028,
        summary = "Evaluates tool calls against a policy in which a deny rule always beats an allow rule, and a call with no matching allow is refused.",
        details = "The policy is a list of rules with a scope. The checker prints the decision and the reason for each request, so the policy can be reviewed like code.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as permissions.py.
            2. Run it: python3 permissions.py
        """,
        example = """
            # Each rule: effect, tool, and scope (None means any scope).
            POLICY = [
                ("deny", "send_email", "external"),   # no mail to outside addresses
                ("allow", "search", None),
                ("allow", "read_file", "project"),    # only inside the project folder
                ("allow", "send_email", "internal"),
                ("allow", "send_email", None),        # a broad allow does not beat a deny
            ]

            def decide(tool, scope):
                matches = [effect for effect, rule_tool, rule_scope in POLICY
                           if rule_tool == tool and rule_scope in (None, scope)]
                if "deny" in matches:
                    return "deny: matched a deny rule"
                if "allow" in matches:
                    return "allow"
                return "deny: no rule allows it"

            requests = [
                ("search", "web"),
                ("read_file", "project"),
                ("read_file", "home"),
                ("send_email", "internal"),
                ("send_email", "external"),
                ("delete_file", "project"),
            ]
            for tool, scope in requests:
                print(f"{tool} in {scope}: {decide(tool, scope)}")
        """,
    ),

    entry(
        databaseId = 9,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Supply chain",
        title = "An SBOM writer for a lock file",
        originalTitle = "Writing a CycloneDX bill of materials",
        author = "Written as a teaching example",
        year = 2027,
        summary = "Reads a simplified lock file and writes a CycloneDX bill of materials, sorted by name, with the hash of each component.",
        details = "The lock file here is a dictionary with placeholder hashes, so the example runs without a network. The output has the shape of a real CycloneDX document, and the example prints the first component in full.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as sbom.py.
            2. Run it: python3 sbom.py
        """,
        example = """
            import json

            # A simplified lock file. The hashes are placeholders, not real digests.
            LOCK = {
                "packages": [
                    {"name": "requests", "version": "2.32.3", "sha256": "ab12"},
                    {"name": "certifi", "version": "2024.8.30", "sha256": "cd34"},
                    {"name": "idna", "version": "3.7", "sha256": "ef56"},
                ]
            }

            def sbom(lock, project):
                components = [
                    {
                        "type": "library",
                        "name": package["name"],
                        "version": package["version"],
                        "hashes": [{"alg": "SHA-256", "content": package["sha256"]}],
                    }
                    for package in sorted(lock["packages"], key=lambda package: package["name"])
                ]
                return {
                    "bomFormat": "CycloneDX",
                    "specVersion": "1.5",
                    "metadata": {"component": {"type": "application", "name": project}},
                    "components": components,
                }

            bom = sbom(LOCK, "example-app")
            print(bom["bomFormat"], bom["specVersion"], "with", len(bom["components"]), "components")
            print(json.dumps(bom["components"][0], sort_keys=True))
            for component in bom["components"]:
                print(f"  {component['name']} {component['version']} {component['hashes'][0]['content']}")
        """,
    ),
)

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data/seed/SeedEntry.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/**
 * Builds one catalogue record. databaseId says which database the record belongs to and defaults to database 1.
 * Room assigns the record id on insert.
 * Instructions and examples are left-aligned with trimIndent().
 * Two markers are replaced inside instructions and examples: <TAB> becomes a tab character (needed for Makefiles),
 * and <DOLLAR> becomes a dollar sign (needed for Perl, PHP and shell code, which would otherwise start a template
 * inside a raw string).
 */
internal fun entry(
    kind: Kind,
    section: String,
    title: String,
    originalTitle: String,
    author: String,
    year: Int,
    summary: String,
    details: String,
    instructions: String? = null,
    example: String? = null,
    rare: Boolean = false,
    databaseId: Long = 1,
): RecordEntity = RecordEntity(
    databaseId = databaseId,
    kind = kind,
    section = section,
    title = title,
    originalTitle = originalTitle,
    author = author,
    year = year,
    summary = summary,
    details = details,
    instructions = instructions?.trimIndent()?.replaceMarkers(),
    example = example?.trimIndent()?.replaceMarkers(),
    rare = rare,
)

private fun String.replaceMarkers(): String =
    replace("<TAB>", "\t").replace("<DOLLAR>", "\$")

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/ui/AppNavHost.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.ui

import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.navigation.NavType
import androidx.navigation.compose.NavHost
import androidx.navigation.compose.composable
import androidx.navigation.compose.rememberNavController
import androidx.navigation.navArgument
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.screens.DatabasesScreen
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.screens.RecordDetailScreen
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.screens.RecordsScreen

private object Route {
    const val DATABASES = "databases"
    const val RECORDS = "records/{databaseId}"
    const val RECORD = "record/{recordId}"
}

@Composable
fun AppNavHost() {
    val navController = rememberNavController()

    NavHost(navController = navController, startDestination = Route.DATABASES) {
        composable(Route.DATABASES) {
            DatabasesScreen(
                onOpenDatabase = { databaseId -> navController.navigate("records/$databaseId") },
            )
        }

        composable(
            route = Route.RECORDS,
            arguments = listOf(navArgument("databaseId") { type = NavType.LongType }),
        ) { entry ->
            RecordsScreen(
                databaseId = entry.arguments?.getLong("databaseId") ?: 0L,
                onBack = { navController.popBackStack() },
                onOpenRecord = { recordId -> navController.navigate("record/$recordId") },
            )
        }

        composable(
            route = Route.RECORD,
            arguments = listOf(navArgument("recordId") { type = NavType.LongType }),
        ) { entry ->
            RecordDetailScreen(
                recordId = entry.arguments?.getLong("recordId") ?: 0L,
                onBack = { navController.popBackStack() },
            )
        }
    }
}

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/ui/LibraryViewModel.kt

package com.example.retrodatabases.ui

import android.app.Application
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.AppDatabase
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.DatabaseEntity
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.DatabaseSummary
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SharingStarted
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.map
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.stateIn
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

/** Data source for all screens: database lists, catalogue records and favorites. */
class LibraryViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {

    private val dao = AppDatabase.get(application).libraryDao()

    val databases: StateFlow<List<DatabaseSummary>> = dao.observeDatabases()
        .stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), emptyList())

    fun database(databaseId: Long): Flow<DatabaseEntity?> = dao.observeDatabase(databaseId)

    /** Records of a database in catalogue order: kind, section, year, title. */
    fun records(databaseId: Long): Flow<List<RecordEntity>> =
        dao.observeRecords(databaseId).map { records -> records.sortedWith(CatalogOrder) }

    fun record(recordId: Long): Flow<RecordEntity?> = dao.observeRecord(recordId)

    fun toggleFavorite(recordId: Long) {
        viewModelScope.launch { dao.toggleFavorite(recordId) }
    }
}

private val CatalogOrder: Comparator<RecordEntity> =
    compareBy<RecordEntity> { it.kind.ordinal }
        .thenBy { it.section }
        .thenBy { it.year }
        .thenBy { it.title }

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/ui/RecordFilter.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.ui

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/**
 * Filters records in the app: kind, favorites, rare records and text search.
 * Search ignores case. SQLite LIKE folds case only for ASCII, so the text is lowercased in Kotlin instead.
 */
fun filterRecords(
    records: List<RecordEntity>,
    query: String,
    kind: Kind?,
    favoritesOnly: Boolean,
    rareOnly: Boolean,
): List<RecordEntity> {
    val needle = query.trim().lowercase()
    return records.filter { record ->
        (kind == null || record.kind == kind) &&
            (!favoritesOnly || record.favorite) &&
            (!rareOnly || record.rare) &&
            (needle.isEmpty() || record.searchableText().contains(needle))
    }
}

private fun RecordEntity.searchableText(): String =
    listOf(title, originalTitle, author, section, summary, year.toString())
        .joinToString(separator = " ")
        .lowercase()

/**
 * Catalogue record card: a coloured kind stripe, badges, title, original title,
 * short description and the favorite button.
 */
@Composable
fun RecordCard(
    record: RecordEntity,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    onToggleFavorite: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    Card(
        onClick = onClick,
        modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    ) {
        Row(modifier = Modifier.height(IntrinsicSize.Min)) {
            Box(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .width(6.dp)
                    .fillMaxHeight()
                    .background(record.kind.accent()),
            )
            Column(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .weight(1f)
                    .padding(start = 14.dp, top = 12.dp, bottom = 12.dp),
                verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(4.dp),
            ) {
                Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
                    KindBadge(kind = record.kind)
                    if (record.rare) {
                        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(6.dp))
                        RareBadge()
                    }
                    Spacer(modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
                    Text(
                        text = record.year.toString(),
                        style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge,
                        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
                    )
                }
                Text(
                    text = record.title,
                    style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium,
                    fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold,
                )
                Text(
                    text = record.summary,
                    style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
                    color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
                    maxLines = 2,
                    overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
                )
            }
            IconButton(onClick = onToggleFavorite) {
                Icon(
                    imageVector = Icons.Filled.Star,
                    contentDescription = stringResource(
                        if (record.favorite) R.string.favorite_remove else R.string.favorite_add,
                    ),
                    tint = if (record.favorite) {
                        MaterialTheme.colorScheme.tertiary
                    } else {
                        MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant.copy(alpha = 0.5f)
                    },
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

/** Screen for one catalogue record: year, kind, section, summary, instructions and a code example. */
@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)
@Composable
fun RecordDetailScreen(
    recordId: Long,
    onBack: () -> Unit,
    viewModel: LibraryViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val record by remember(recordId) { viewModel.record(recordId) }
        .collectAsStateWithLifecycle(initialValue = null)
    val current = record

    Scaffold(
        topBar = {
            TopAppBar(
                title = { Text(text = current?.section.orEmpty(), maxLines = 1) },
                navigationIcon = {
                    IconButton(onClick = onBack) {
                        Icon(
                            imageVector = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack,
                            contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.cd_back),
                        )
                    }
                },
                actions = {
                    if (current != null) {
                        IconButton(onClick = { viewModel.toggleFavorite(current.id) }) {
                            Icon(
                                imageVector = Icons.Filled.Star,
                                contentDescription = stringResource(
                                    if (current.favorite) R.string.favorite_remove else R.string.favorite_add,
                                ),
                                tint = if (current.favorite) {
                                    MaterialTheme.colorScheme.tertiary
                                } else {
                                    MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
                                },
                            )
                        }
                    }
                },
            )
        },
    ) { innerPadding ->
        if (current != null) {
            RecordDetailContent(record = current, modifier = Modifier.padding(innerPadding))
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun RecordDetailContent(record: RecordEntity, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    Column(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
            .padding(horizontal = 16.dp, vertical = 8.dp),
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp),
    ) {
        Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(6.dp)) {
            Text(
                text = "${stringResource(R.string.label_year)} ${record.year}",
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium,
                fontWeight = FontWeight.Black,
                color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary,
            )
            Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
                KindBadge(kind = record.kind)
                if (record.rare) {
                    RareBadge()
                }
            }
            Text(
                text = record.title,
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall,
                fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold,
            )
            Text(
                text = record.originalTitle,
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleSmall,
                color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
            )
            Text(
                text = "${stringResource(R.string.label_author)}: ${record.author}",
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
            )
        }

        InfoSection(title = stringResource(R.string.section_summary)) {
            Text(text = record.summary, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
        }
        InfoSection(title = stringResource(R.string.section_details)) {
            Text(text = record.details, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
        }
        record.instructions?.let { instructions ->
            InfoSection(title = stringResource(R.string.section_instructions)) {
                Text(text = instructions, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
            }
        }
        record.example?.let { example ->
            InfoSection(title = stringResource(R.string.section_example)) {
                CodeBlock(code = example)
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun InfoSection(title: String, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit) {
    Card(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
        Column(
            modifier = Modifier.padding(16.dp),
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
        ) {
            Text(
                text = title.uppercase(),
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge,
                color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary,
            )
            content()
        }
    }
}

/** Monospaced code block; long lines scroll horizontally. */
@Composable
private fun CodeBlock(code: String) {
    Surface(
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        shape = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp),
        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background,
    ) {
        Text(
            text = code,
            modifier = Modifier
                .horizontalScroll(rememberScrollState())
                .padding(12.dp),
            style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
            fontFamily = FontFamily.Monospace,
            softWrap = false,
        )
    }
}

package com.example.retrodatabases.ui.screens

import androidx.compose.foundation.background
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement

import androidx.lifecycle.compose.collectAsStateWithLifecycle

import com.example.retrodatabases.R
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.LibraryViewModel
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.components.RecordCard
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.filterRecords
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.theme.accent

/**
 * Catalogue of one database: search, filters by kind, favorites and rare records.
 * Records are grouped by section within each kind.
 */
@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)
@Composable
fun RecordsScreen(
    databaseId: Long,
    onBack: () -> Unit,
    onOpenRecord: (Long) -> Unit,
    viewModel: LibraryViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val database by remember(databaseId) { viewModel.database(databaseId) }
        .collectAsStateWithLifecycle(initialValue = null)
    val records by remember(databaseId) { viewModel.records(databaseId) }
        .collectAsStateWithLifecycle(initialValue = emptyList())

    var query by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") }
    var kind by remember { mutableStateOf<Kind?>(null) }
    var favoritesOnly by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    var rareOnly by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

    val countByKind = remember(records) { records.groupingBy { it.kind }.eachCount() }
    val visible = remember(records, query, kind, favoritesOnly, rareOnly) {
        filterRecords(records, query, kind, favoritesOnly, rareOnly)
    }
    // Group order is kept: records are already sorted by kind and section
    val groups = remember(visible) { visible.groupBy { it.kind to it.section } }

    Scaffold(
        topBar = {
            TopAppBar(
                title = {
                    Text(
                        text = database?.name.orEmpty(),
                        style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium,
                        maxLines = 1,
                    )
                },
                navigationIcon = {
                    IconButton(onClick = onBack) {
                        Icon(
                            imageVector = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack,
                            contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.cd_back),
                        )
                    }
                },
            )
        },
    ) { innerPadding ->
        Column(
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .padding(innerPadding),
        ) {
            OutlinedTextField(
                value = query,
                onValueChange = { query = it },
                modifier = Modifier
                    .fillMaxWidth()
                    .padding(horizontal = 16.dp),
                singleLine = true,
                placeholder = { Text(stringResource(R.string.search_hint)) },
                leadingIcon = { Icon(Icons.Filled.Search, contentDescription = null) },
                trailingIcon = {
                    if (query.isNotEmpty()) {
                        IconButton(onClick = { query = "" }) {
                            Icon(
                                imageVector = Icons.Filled.Close,
                                contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.cd_clear),
                            )
                        }
                    }
                },
            )

            LazyRow(
                modifier = Modifier.padding(vertical = 12.dp),
                contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 16.dp),
                horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
            ) {
                item {
                    FilterChip(
                        selected = kind == null && !favoritesOnly && !rareOnly,
                        onClick = {
                            kind = null
                            favoritesOnly = false
                            rareOnly = false
                        },
                        label = { Text("${stringResource(R.string.filter_all)} ${records.size}") },
                    )
                }
                items(Kind.entries, key = { it.name }) { option ->
                    FilterChip(
                        selected = kind == option,
                        onClick = { kind = if (kind == option) null else option },
                        label = { Text("${option.label} ${countByKind[option] ?: 0}") },
                    )
                }
                item {
                    FilterChip(
                        selected = favoritesOnly,
                        onClick = { favoritesOnly = !favoritesOnly },
                        label = { Text(stringResource(R.string.filter_favorites)) },
                        leadingIcon = { Icon(Icons.Filled.Star, contentDescription = null) },
                    )
                }
                item {
                    FilterChip(
                        selected = rareOnly,
                        onClick = { rareOnly = !rareOnly },
                        label = { Text("${stringResource(R.string.filter_rare)} ${records.count { it.rare }}") },
                    )
                }
            }

            Text(
                text = stringResource(R.string.found_count, visible.size),
                modifier = Modifier.padding(horizontal = 16.dp, vertical = 4.dp),
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge,
                color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
            )

            if (visible.isEmpty()) {
                Text(
                    text = stringResource(R.string.nothing_found),
                    modifier = Modifier.padding(24.dp),
                    style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge,
                    color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
                )
            } else {
                LazyColumn(
                    modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
                    contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 16.dp, vertical = 8.dp),
                    verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(10.dp),
                ) {
                    groups.forEach { (group, sectionRecords) ->
                        val (groupKind, groupSection) = group
                        item(key = "header-${groupKind.name}-$groupSection") {
                            SectionHeader(
                                title = groupSection,
                                count = sectionRecords.size,
                                accent = groupKind.accent(),
                            )
                        }
                        items(sectionRecords, key = { it.id }) { record ->
                            RecordCard(
                                record = record,
                                onClick = { onOpenRecord(record.id) },
                                onToggleFavorite = { viewModel.toggleFavorite(record.id) },
                            )
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/** Section header inside a kind: a coloured bar, the section name and the record count. */
@Composable
private fun SectionHeader(title: String, count: Int, accent: Color) {
    Row(
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .padding(top = 8.dp, bottom = 2.dp),
        verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
    ) {
        Box(
            modifier = Modifier
                .size(width = 4.dp, height = 18.dp)
                .clip(RoundedCornerShape(2.dp))
                .background(accent),
        )
        Text(
            text = title,
            modifier = Modifier.padding(start = 10.dp),
            style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleSmall,
            fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold,
            color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface,
        )
        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
        Text(
            text = count.toString(),
            style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge,
            color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
        )
    }
}

package com.example.retrodatabases.ui.theme

import android.graphics.Color as AndroidColor
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind

/** Colour of a record kind: the stripe on a card, the badge background and the section header. */
fun Kind.accent(): Color = when (this) {
    Kind.LANGUAGE -> Color(0xFF4DD0E1)
    Kind.SYSTEM -> Color(0xFF7986CB)
    Kind.DEVICE -> Color(0xFFFFB74D)
    Kind.TOOL -> Color(0xFF81C784)
    Kind.PRACTICE -> Color(0xFFBA68C8)
    Kind.GUIDE -> Color(0xFF64B5F6)
    Kind.EXAMPLE -> Color(0xFFFFF176)
    Kind.PROJECT -> Color(0xFFA1887F)
    Kind.FLEX -> Color(0xFFE57373)
    Kind.CROSS -> Color(0xFFF06292)
}

/** Converts a #RRGGBB string from the database into a Compose colour. */
fun parseHexColor(hex: String): Color = Color(AndroidColor.parseColor(hex))

package com.example.retrodatabases.ui.theme

import androidx.compose.foundation.isSystemInDarkTheme

import androidx.compose.material3.lightColorScheme
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color

/** Dark theme in the spirit of 80s terminals: dark background and bright accents. */
private val DarkColors = darkColorScheme(
    primary = Color(0xFF4DD0E1),
    onPrimary = Color(0xFF00363D),
    primaryContainer = Color(0xFF004F58),
    onPrimaryContainer = Color(0xFFA5EEF9),
    secondary = Color(0xFFF06292),
    onSecondary = Color(0xFF5C0A2C),
    tertiary = Color(0xFFFFB74D),
    onTertiary = Color(0xFF4A2800),
    background = Color(0xFF0E1116),
    onBackground = Color(0xFFE1E6EE),
    surface = Color(0xFF151A21),
    onSurface = Color(0xFFE1E6EE),
    surfaceVariant = Color(0xFF232B36),
    onSurfaceVariant = Color(0xFFB7C0CC),
    outline = Color(0xFF5B6675),
)

private val LightColors = lightColorScheme(
    primary = Color(0xFF00677A),
    onPrimary = Color.White,
    primaryContainer = Color(0xFFA5EEF9),
    onPrimaryContainer = Color(0xFF001F25),
    secondary = Color(0xFFB0215C),
    onSecondary = Color.White,
    tertiary = Color(0xFF8A5100),
    onTertiary = Color.White,
    background = Color(0xFFF7F9FC),
    onBackground = Color(0xFF191C20),
    surface = Color(0xFFFFFFFF),
    onSurface = Color(0xFF191C20),
    surfaceVariant = Color(0xFFDDE3EA),
    onSurfaceVariant = Color(0xFF41484F),
    outline = Color(0xFF71787F),
)

@Composable
fun RetroDatabasesTheme(
    darkTheme: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(),
    content: @Composable () -> Unit,
) {
    MaterialTheme(
        colorScheme = if (darkTheme) DarkColors else LightColors,
        content = content,
    )
}

    @Test
    fun migrationRestoresDatabaseTwoAndKeepsDatabaseOne() = runBlocking {
        val context = ApplicationProvider.getApplicationContext<Context>()
        val database = AppDatabase.get(context)
        val dao = database.libraryDao()
        val sqlite = database.openHelper.writableDatabase

        // A file made at version 1 has no database 2: remove it, then run the migration.
        sqlite.execSQL("DELETE FROM records WHERE databaseId = 2")
        sqlite.execSQL("DELETE FROM databases WHERE id = 2")
        MIGRATION_1_2.migrate(sqlite)

        assertEquals(seedDatabases.size, dao.observeDatabases().first().size)
        assertEquals(db2Records.size, dao.observeRecords(2L).first().size)
        assertEquals(db1Records.size, dao.observeRecords(1L).first().size)
    }

    @Test
    fun toggleFavoriteStoresTheChange() = runBlocking {
        val context = ApplicationProvider.getApplicationContext<Context>()
        val dao = AppDatabase.get(context).libraryDao()

        val record = dao.observeRecords(1L).first().first()
        assertEquals(false, record.favorite)

        dao.toggleFavorite(record.id)
        val updated = dao.observeRecord(record.id).first()
        assertNotNull(updated)
        assertEquals(true, updated!!.favorite)
    }

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/test/java/com/example/retrodatabases/RecordFilterTest.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity
import com.example.retrodatabases.ui.filterRecords
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Test

class RecordFilterTest {

    private val records = listOf(
        record(1, Kind.PRACTICE, "Structured programming", "Structured programming", 1972, favorite = true),
        record(2, Kind.LANGUAGE, "C language", "C", 1972),
        record(3, Kind.PRACTICE, "Boundary value analysis", "Boundary value analysis", 1979, rare = true),
    )

    @Test
    fun emptyQueryReturnsEverything() {
        assertEquals(listOf(1L, 2L, 3L), filterRecords(records, "", null, false, false).map { it.id })
    }

    @Test
    fun searchIsCaseInsensitive() {
        assertEquals(listOf(1L), filterRecords(records, "STRUCTURED", null, false, false).map { it.id })
    }

    @Test
    fun searchMatchesOriginalTitleAndYear() {
        assertEquals(listOf(3L), filterRecords(records, "boundary", null, false, false).map { it.id })
        assertEquals(listOf(3L), filterRecords(records, "1979", null, false, false).map { it.id })
    }

    @Test
    fun kindFilterKeepsOnlyThatKind() {
        assertEquals(listOf(2L), filterRecords(records, "", Kind.LANGUAGE, false, false).map { it.id })
    }

    @Test
    fun favoritesAndRareFiltersCombine() {
        assertEquals(listOf(1L), filterRecords(records, "", null, true, false).map { it.id })
        assertEquals(listOf(3L), filterRecords(records, "", null, false, true).map { it.id })
        assertEquals(emptyList<Long>(), filterRecords(records, "", null, true, true).map { it.id })
    }

    private fun record(
        id: Long,
        kind: Kind,
        title: String,
        originalTitle: String,
        year: Int,
        favorite: Boolean = false,
        rare: Boolean = false,
    ) = RecordEntity(
        id = id,
        databaseId = 1,
        kind = kind,
        section = "Section",
        title = title,
        originalTitle = originalTitle,
        author = "Author",
        year = year,
        summary = "Short summary",
        details = "Details",
        instructions = null,
        example = null,
        rare = rare,
        favorite = favorite,
    )
}

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed.db34Records

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed.seedRecords
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals

class SeedDataTest {

    private val catalogues = listOf(
        db1Records, db2Records, db3Records, db4Records, db5Records, db6Records, db7Records, db8Records, db9Records,
        db10Records, db11Records, db12Records, db13Records, db14Records,
        db15Records, db16Records, db17Records, db18Records, db19Records,
        db20Records, db21Records, db22Records, db23Records, db24Records, db25Records, db26Records,
        db27Records, db28Records, db29Records, db30Records, db31Records, db32Records, db33Records, db34Records,
    )

    @Test
    fun seededDatabasesHaveUniqueIdsAndTheirOwnRecords() {
        val ids = seedDatabases.map { it.id }
        assertEquals(ids.size, ids.toSet().size)
        assertTrue(seedRecords.all { it.databaseId in ids })
        assertTrue(db1Records.all { it.databaseId == 1L })
        assertTrue(db2Records.all { it.databaseId == 2L })
        assertTrue(db3Records.all { it.databaseId == 3L })
        assertTrue(db4Records.all { it.databaseId == 4L })
        assertTrue(db5Records.all { it.databaseId == 5L })
        assertTrue(db6Records.all { it.databaseId == 6L })
        assertTrue(db7Records.all { it.databaseId == 7L })
        assertTrue(db8Records.all { it.databaseId == 8L })
        assertTrue(db9Records.all { it.databaseId == 9L })
        assertTrue(db10Records.all { it.databaseId == 10L })
        assertTrue(db11Records.all { it.databaseId == 11L })
        assertTrue(db12Records.all { it.databaseId == 12L })
        assertTrue(db13Records.all { it.databaseId == 13L })
        assertTrue(db14Records.all { it.databaseId == 14L })
        assertTrue(db15Records.all { it.databaseId == 15L })
        assertTrue(db16Records.all { it.databaseId == 16L })
        assertTrue(db17Records.all { it.databaseId == 17L })
        assertTrue(db18Records.all { it.databaseId == 18L })
        assertTrue(db19Records.all { it.databaseId == 19L })
        assertTrue(db20Records.all { it.databaseId == 20L })
        assertTrue(db21Records.all { it.databaseId == 21L })
        assertTrue(db22Records.all { it.databaseId == 22L })
        assertTrue(db23Records.all { it.databaseId == 23L })
        assertTrue(db24Records.all { it.databaseId == 24L })
        assertTrue(db25Records.all { it.databaseId == 25L })
        assertTrue(db26Records.all { it.databaseId == 26L })
        assertTrue(db27Records.all { it.databaseId == 27L })
        assertTrue(db28Records.all { it.databaseId == 28L })
        assertTrue(db29Records.all { it.databaseId == 29L })
        assertTrue(db30Records.all { it.databaseId == 30L })
        assertTrue(db31Records.all { it.databaseId == 31L })
        assertTrue(db32Records.all { it.databaseId == 32L })
        assertTrue(db33Records.all { it.databaseId == 33L })
        assertTrue(db34Records.all { it.databaseId == 34L })
    }

    @Test
    fun titlesAreUniqueWithinEachDatabase() {
        for (records in catalogues) {
            val titles = records.map { it.title }
            assertEquals(titles.size, titles.toSet().size)
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun yearsAreInTheRangeOfEachCatalogue() {
        assertTrue(db1Records.all { it.year in 1950..1990 })
        assertTrue(db2Records.all { it.year in 1990..1999 })
        assertTrue(db3Records.all { it.year in 2000..2010 })
        assertTrue(db4Records.all { it.year in 2010..2020 })
        assertTrue(db5Records.all { it.year in 2020..2026 })
        assertTrue(db6Records.all { it.year in 1950..1960 })
        assertTrue(db7Records.all { it.year in 1960..1970 })
        assertTrue(db8Records.all { it.year in 1970..1980 })
        assertTrue(db9Records.all { it.year in 2026..2036 })
        assertTrue(db10Records.all { it.year in 1940..1950 })
        assertTrue(db11Records.all { it.year in 1930..1940 })
        assertTrue(db12Records.all { it.year in 1920..1930 })
        assertTrue(db13Records.all { it.year in 1910..1920 })
        assertTrue(db14Records.all { it.year in 1900..1910 })
        assertTrue(db15Records.all { it.year in 1890..1900 })
        assertTrue(db16Records.all { it.year in 1880..1890 })
        assertTrue(db17Records.all { it.year in 1870..1880 })
        assertTrue(db18Records.all { it.year in 1860..1870 })
        assertTrue(db19Records.all { it.year in 1850..1860 })
        assertTrue(db20Records.all { it.year in 1840..1850 })
        assertTrue(db21Records.all { it.year in 1830..1840 })
        assertTrue(db22Records.all { it.year in 1820..1830 })
        assertTrue(db23Records.all { it.year in 1810..1820 })
        assertTrue(db24Records.all { it.year in 1800..1810 })
        assertTrue(db25Records.all { it.year in 1790..1800 })
        assertTrue(db26Records.all { it.year in 1780..1790 })
        assertTrue(db27Records.all { it.year in 1770..1780 })
        assertTrue(db28Records.all { it.year in 1760..1770 })
        assertTrue(db29Records.all { it.year in 1750..1760 })
        assertTrue(db30Records.all { it.year in 1740..1750 })
        assertTrue(db31Records.all { it.year in 1730..1740 })
        assertTrue(db32Records.all { it.year in 1720..1730 })
        assertTrue(db33Records.all { it.year in 1710..1720 })
        assertTrue(db34Records.all { it.year in 1700..1710 })
    }

    @Test
    fun everyKindHasRecordsInEachDatabase() {
        for (records in catalogues) {
            assertEquals(Kind.entries.toSet(), records.map { it.kind }.toSet())
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun everyRecordHasSummaryAndDetails() {
        assertTrue(seedRecords.all { it.summary.isNotBlank() && it.details.isNotBlank() })
    }

    @Test
    fun projectsHaveInstructionsAndCode() {
        val projects = seedRecords.filter { it.kind == Kind.PROJECT }
        assertTrue(projects.isNotEmpty())
        assertTrue(projects.all { !it.instructions.isNullOrBlank() && !it.example.isNullOrBlank() })
    }

    @Test
    fun rareRecordsArePresentInEachDatabase() {
        for (records in catalogues) {
            assertTrue(records.count { it.rare } > 0)
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun forecastEntriesSayTheyAreForecasts() {
        val forecastKinds = setOf(Kind.LANGUAGE, Kind.SYSTEM, Kind.DEVICE, Kind.TOOL, Kind.PRACTICE)
        val forecasts = db9Records.filter { it.kind in forecastKinds }
        assertTrue(forecasts.isNotEmpty())
        assertTrue(forecasts.all { it.details.contains("forecast", ignoreCase = true) })
    }
}

# FILE: RetroDatabases/gradlew
################################################################################
#!/bin/sh

#
# Copyright © 2015-2021 the original authors.
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
#      https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
# limitations under the License.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#

##############################################################################
#
#   Gradle start up script for POSIX generated by Gradle.
#
#   Important for running:
#
#   (1) You need a POSIX-compliant shell to run this script. If your /bin/sh is
#       noncompliant, but you have some other compliant shell such as ksh or
#       bash, then to run this script, type that shell name before the whole
#       command line, like:
#
#           ksh Gradle
#
#       Busybox and similar reduced shells will NOT work, because this script
#       requires all of these POSIX shell features:
#         * functions;
#         * expansions «$var», «${var}», «${var:-default}», «${var+SET}»,
#           «${var#prefix}», «${var%suffix}», and «$( cmd )»;
#         * compound commands having a testable exit status, especially «case»;
#         * various built-in commands including «command», «set», and «ulimit».
#
#   Important for patching:
#
#   (2) This script targets any POSIX shell, so it avoids extensions provided
#       by Bash, Ksh, etc; in particular arrays are avoided.
#
#       The "traditional" practice of packing multiple parameters into a
#       space-separated string is a well documented source of bugs and security
#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.
#
#       Where the inherited environment variables (DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS,
#       and GRADLE_OPTS) rely on word-splitting, this is performed explicitly;
#       see the in-line comments for details.
#
#       There are tweaks for specific operating systems such as AIX, CygWin,
#       Darwin, MinGW, and NonStop.
#
#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/HEAD/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac

CLASSPATH="\\\"\\\""


# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )
    CLASSPATH=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$CLASSPATH" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi
        # Roll the args list around exactly as many times as the number of
        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.
        #
        # NB: a `for` loop captures its iteration list before it begins, so
        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -classpath "$CLASSPATH" \
        -jar "$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar" \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"

@if "%DEBUG%"=="" @echo off
@rem ##########################################################################
@rem
@rem  Gradle startup script for Windows
@rem
@rem ##########################################################################

@rem Set local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" setlocal

set DIRNAME=%~dp0
if "%DIRNAME%"=="" set DIRNAME=.
@rem This is normally unused
set APP_BASE_NAME=%~n0
set APP_HOME=%DIRNAME%

@rem Resolve any "." and ".." in APP_HOME to make it shorter.
for %%i in ("%APP_HOME%") do set APP_HOME=%%~fi

@rem Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
set DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS="-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"

@rem Find java.exe
if defined JAVA_HOME goto findJavaFromJavaHome

set JAVA_EXE=java.exe
%JAVA_EXE% -version >NUL 2>&1
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 goto execute

echo. 1>&2
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH. 1>&2
echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:findJavaFromJavaHome
set JAVA_HOME=%JAVA_HOME:"=%
set JAVA_EXE=%JAVA_HOME%/bin/java.exe

if exist "%JAVA_EXE%" goto execute

echo. 1>&2
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: %JAVA_HOME% 1>&2
echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:execute
@rem Setup the command line

set CLASSPATH=


@rem Execute Gradle
"%JAVA_EXE%" %DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS% %JAVA_OPTS% %GRADLE_OPTS% "-Dorg.gradle.appname=%APP_BASE_NAME%" -classpath "%CLASSPATH%" -jar "%APP_HOME%\gradle\wrapper\gradle-wrapper.jar" %*

:end
@rem End local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 goto mainEnd

:fail
rem Set variable GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE if you need the _script_ return code instead of
rem the _cmd.exe /c_ return code!
set EXIT_CODE=%ERRORLEVEL%
if %EXIT_CODE% equ 0 set EXIT_CODE=1
if not ""=="%GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE%" exit %EXIT_CODE%
exit /b %EXIT_CODE%

:mainEnd
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" endlocal

:omega
